tool.name: BuildFlowMapPage
tool.summary: Write a self-contained flow-map page, and optionally add the flows to the map for the Time Slider.

param.name: flows
param.dialogReference: The table that holds one row per flow: where it starts, where it goes, and optionally how much, when, and in which group. A layer, a feature class, a standalone table, a CSV, a JSON or a GeoJSON all work. Pick it first: every column list below is filled with its columns, and nothing is chosen for you - each field is yours to pick.
param.pythonReference: The table that holds one row per flow: where it starts, where it goes, and optionally how much, when, and in which group. A layer, a feature class, a standalone table, a CSV, a JSON or a GeoJSON all work. Pick it first: every column list below is filled with its columns, and nothing is chosen for you - each field is yours to pick.

param.name: out_folder
param.dialogReference: The folder the page is written to. Browse to it: a folder you can navigate to, not a path to type. index.html is written inside it, or the name given in 'Page file name'. Missing folders are created.
param.pythonReference: The folder the page is written to. Browse to it: a folder you can navigate to, not a path to type. index.html is written inside it, or the name given in 'Page file name'. Missing folders are created.

param.name: page_name
param.dialogReference: The name of the HTML file, written inside the output folder. Leave it empty for index.html. A name without .html gets it added.
param.pythonReference: The name of the HTML file, written inside the output folder. Leave it empty for index.html. A name without .html gets it added.

param.name: o_name
param.dialogReference: The column holding the place a flow starts from. Leave it empty when the table has no separate column for it: the origin is then labelled by its coordinates, which is what it is, and the flow stays a line between two points. Not needed at all when a places layer or an outlines layer can locate the names.
param.pythonReference: The column holding the place a flow starts from. Leave it empty when the table has no separate column for it: the origin is then labelled by its coordinates, which is what it is, and the flow stays a line between two points. Not needed at all when a places layer or an outlines layer can locate the names.

param.name: d_name
param.dialogReference: The column holding the place a flow goes to. Empty: the origin column is used for both ends, and a row whose two coordinate pairs are the same point counts as a record inside that place. When the origins and destinations are told apart by their coordinates rather than by their names, either put the same column in both name fields - the two positions stay two dots - or leave the origin name empty: its end is then labelled by its position and the flow is still a line.
param.pythonReference: The column holding the place a flow goes to. Empty: the origin column is used for both ends, and a row whose two coordinate pairs are the same point counts as a record inside that place. When the origins and destinations are told apart by their coordinates rather than by their names, either put the same column in both name fields - the two positions stay two dots - or leave the origin name empty: its end is then labelled by its position and the flow is still a line.

param.name: value
param.dialogReference: The column holding the quantity to draw - households, people, cases, MILDA, tonnes. It must contain numbers: a column of text codes is refused by name. Leave it empty and every row counts 1.
param.pythonReference: The column holding the quantity to draw - households, people, cases, MILDA, tonnes. It must contain numbers: a column of text codes is refused by name. Leave it empty and every row counts 1.

param.name: date
param.dialogReference: The column holding the date, or a plain day number, that drives the animation. Leave it empty and everything happens on one day.
param.pythonReference: The column holding the date, or a plain day number, that drives the animation. Leave it empty and everything happens on one day.

param.name: o_lon
param.dialogReference: The longitude of the place a flow starts from, in degrees (WGS84). A column in metres is reported as an error rather than drawn off the map.
param.pythonReference: The longitude of the place a flow starts from, in degrees (WGS84). A column in metres is reported as an error rather than drawn off the map.

param.name: o_lat
param.dialogReference: The latitude of the place a flow starts from, in degrees (WGS84). The tool checks that this column and the longitude column are the right way round, and swaps them if they are not.
param.pythonReference: The latitude of the place a flow starts from, in degrees (WGS84). The tool checks that this column and the longitude column are the right way round, and swaps them if they are not.

param.name: d_lon
param.dialogReference: The longitude of the place a flow goes to, in degrees. Leave empty when the destination is the origin.
param.pythonReference: The longitude of the place a flow goes to, in degrees. Leave empty when the destination is the origin.

param.name: d_lat
param.dialogReference: The latitude of the place a flow goes to, in degrees. Leave empty when the destination is the origin.
param.pythonReference: The latitude of the place a flow goes to, in degrees. Leave empty when the destination is the origin.

param.name: places
param.dialogReference: A point layer giving the coordinates of the names in the flow table, for tables that have no coordinates of their own. Optional.
param.pythonReference: A point layer giving the coordinates of the names in the flow table, for tables that have no coordinates of their own. Optional.

param.name: places_name
param.displayname: Name field in the places layer
param.dialogReference: The column of the places layer that holds the place name: it is matched against the names in the flow table, ignoring case, accents and punctuation.
param.pythonReference: The column of the places layer that holds the place name: it is matched against the names in the flow table, ignoring case, accents and punctuation.

param.name: places_group
param.displayname: Group field in the places layer
param.dialogReference: The column of the places layer that holds the region or group a place belongs to. Optional: it colours the dots.
param.pythonReference: The column of the places layer that holds the region or group a place belongs to. Optional: it colours the dots.

param.name: bounds_fine
param.dialogReference: The detailed outlines (districts, communes, admin 2). They are drawn on the page and their names can locate places. Optional.
param.pythonReference: The detailed outlines (districts, communes, admin 2). They are drawn on the page and their names can locate places. Optional.

param.name: bounds_fine_name
param.dialogReference: The column of the detailed outlines holding the name to match against the flow table. Required when outlines are chosen.
param.pythonReference: The column of the detailed outlines holding the name to match against the flow table. Required when outlines are chosen.

param.name: bounds_coarse
param.dialogReference: The coarse outlines (provinces, governorates, admin 1), drawn under the detailed ones. Optional.
param.pythonReference: The coarse outlines (provinces, governorates, admin 1), drawn under the detailed ones. Optional.

param.name: bounds_coarse_name
param.displayname: Name field in the coarse outlines
param.dialogReference: The column of the coarse outlines holding the name to match against the flow table. Required when coarse outlines are chosen.
param.pythonReference: The column of the coarse outlines holding the name to match against the flow table. Required when coarse outlines are chosen.

param.name: open_page
param.displayname: Open the page when it is written
param.dialogReference: Open the page in the default browser as soon as it is written. The page is a single file: it can be moved, mailed or put on a shared drive and it still works offline.
param.pythonReference: Open the page in the default browser as soon as it is written. The page is a single file: it can be moved, mailed or put on a shared drive and it still works offline.

param.name: title
param.dialogReference: The title written at the top of the page. Empty: the name of the table, cleaned up.
param.pythonReference: The title written at the top of the page. Empty: the name of the table, cleaned up.

param.name: subtitle
param.dialogReference: A second line under the title. Empty: a sentence describing what the dots and lines are.
param.pythonReference: A second line under the title. Empty: a sentence describing what the dots and lines are.

param.name: unit
param.dialogReference: What the values are counted in: households, people, cases, MILDA. Empty: deduced from the value column, or 'records'.
param.pythonReference: What the values are counted in: households, people, cases, MILDA. Empty: deduced from the value column, or 'records'.

param.name: node_label
param.dialogReference: What one dot is called on the page: place, village, district. Empty: 'place'.
param.pythonReference: What one dot is called on the page: place, village, district. Empty: 'place'.

param.name: group_label
param.dialogReference: What a group of dots is called: region, province, area. Empty: 'area' when outlines are given, otherwise 'group'.
param.pythonReference: What a group of dots is called: region, province, area. Empty: 'area' when outlines are given, otherwise 'group'.

param.name: source
param.dialogReference: The credit line at the foot of the page. Empty: the table name and the workspace.
param.pythonReference: The credit line at the foot of the page. Empty: the table name and the workspace.

param.name: add_animation
param.displayname: Add the flows to the map, ready for the Time Slider
param.dialogReference: Also write the flows as a line feature class with a date field, add it to the current map and turn time on, so the Time Slider plays the animation in Pro itself and can export it as a video. The feature class and a .lyrx are saved in the output folder.
param.pythonReference: Also write the flows as a line feature class with a date field, add it to the current map and turn time on, so the Time Slider plays the animation in Pro itself and can export it as a video. The feature class and a .lyrx are saved in the output folder.

param.name: template
param.dialogReference: The page to fill with data: the built index.html. Empty: the index.html next to this toolbox.
param.pythonReference: The page to fill with data: the built index.html. Empty: the index.html next to this toolbox.

param.name: out_json
param.dialogReference: Also write the dataset as JSON, for a script, a database or another page. Optional.
param.pythonReference: Also write the dataset as JSON, for a script, a database or another page. Optional.
